source.title: Dromore Weekly Times and West Down Herald, 21 June 1952, p. 2 ("East Down Rural Council: chairman re-elected for eleventh year"); Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10 ("County and rural council nominations complete"); Belfast News-Letter, 4 June 1949, p. 3 ("Unionist successes in council elections")
source.publisher: Dromore Weekly Times and West Down Herald (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned without a contest: the nominations gave contests only in Downpatrick Rural, Dundrum, Killyleagh Rural and Raholp (Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10); re-elected chairman for his eleventh year at the first monthly meeting of the new council, June 1952 (Dromore Weekly Times, 21 June 1952, p. 2) (round 2, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the 21 electoral divisions of Downpatrick rural district, one member each, polled on 5 June 1952. Twenty-four nominations were lodged; four divisions were contested and one withdrawal left Raholp uncontested. Ardglass and Ballynahinch are recorded from the report of the new council's first monthly meeting (Dromore Weekly Times, 21 June 1952), with their divisions from the 1949 return (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 2 June 1949 return (W. J. M'Coubrey, Ballynahinch); the council-meeting report cited names the member as sitting at the first meeting of the new council. Returned unopposed.
